subject: VaultCorp Hosted API: residency, TTL, and purge commitments Q&A

Subject: Hosted API Qs: residency, TTL, and proof of purge

Jordan —

Thanks again for the demo today. As part of our procurement checklist I need a short, concrete set of answers we can include in our security questionnaire (we'll attach to our procurement packet). The key items:

1) Where are customer request payloads and generated responses stored (region)? Do you support region locking / geofencing for hosted customers?
2) What are default retention windows for request logs, generated tokens, and cached KV entries (if any)? Can these be shortened per-customer?
3) When a customer requests data deletion, what systems are impacted and how do you prove deletion (timestamped audit/event + object-level confirmation)?

I've attached our Q4 appendix with the questionnaire fields. Could you provide answers we can paste into the doc by EOD tomorrow?

Appreciate it —
Ethan

Subject: Re: Hosted API Qs: residency, TTL, and proof of purge

Ethan —

Thanks for the clear list. Below are concise answers you can paste into your questionnaire; I also attached our operational "Method of Procedure" (MOP) that maps deletion paths to systems. Let me know if you want a short attestation signed by our Security team.

1) Data residency / geofencing:
- Customer request payloads and generated outputs for hosted customers are stored in the active serving region (for VaultCorp we propose US-West). We support region preference (region routing) for hosted accounts and can restrict serving + retention to a single AWS region (US-West/US-East) subject to contractual commitment.

2) Retention windows (defaults / per-customer overrides):
- API request/response payloads: default 30 days; configurable down to 0 days (ephemeral) for enterprise plans via contract and RBAC-controlled console settings.
- System logs (ingest/forwarder traces): default 90 days; can be shortened to 30 days on request for enterprise accounts.
- Inference KV/cache entries (prefix caching & KV cache): default eviction is LRU and TTLs vary by model/workload; we persist cache snapshots only when configured for performance; default persisted cache retention is 7 days and can be disabled.

3) Deletion / proof:
- On a deletion request we run a coordinated workflow: remove live objects from serving nodes, invalidate relevant cache entries, delete persisted payloads from primary object stores, and schedule deletion from backups per backup retention policy. Each step emits an audit event with a UUID and timestamp.
- We provide a deletion confirmation package (JSON) containing the UUIDs, affected object keys, timestamps, and storage paths. For contracts requiring a signed attestation we can provide a signed PDF from Security after completing the workflow.

We can also provide a short appendix describing backup retention behavior and the timeline for purge from cold backups (default: 90 days unless shorter retention is contracted). Attaching: redwood_mop_hostedapi_v1.2.pdf

—Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Hosted API Qs: residency, TTL, and proof of purge

Ethan —

Adding a few operational clarifications that VaultCorp tends to ask about:

- Backup snapshots & immutable stores: our cold backups are encrypted and retained per the account-level retention policy. A deletion request triggers a logical deletion marker immediately; physical purging from immutable cold stores follows the backup retention window unless an expedited purge is contractually requested (we'll include the SLA and cost for expedited purge in the contract).

- Cache vs persisted artifacts: ephemeral cache eviction (in-memory/KV) typically takes effect within seconds to minutes. Persisted request/response blobs and any debug traces are removed via the object-store deletion step. The audit package references both the ephemeral cache invalidation UUIDs and the object-store keys so you can correlate events.

- Proof-of-delete for compliance audits: we support exporting the deletion events to your SIEM via secure webhook (HMAC-signed) or S3 push; alternatively we can provide signed attestations plus system logs for a defined period.

Happy to provide the exact log paths and example JSON schema for the deletion package if VaultCorp wants it pasted into the questionnaire.

—Neha
Neha Kapoor
Director, Product Security | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Hosted API Qs: residency, TTL, and proof of purge

Ethan —

Answers inline below and I've attached a signed attestation template we can finalize once VaultCorp confirms region and retention choices.

1) Ephemeral (0 days) behavior:
- For the true "0 days / memory-only" option (offered to enterprise customers by contract) we never persist request/response blobs to long-term object stores. Processing occurs in memory on serving nodes; debug traces are disabled, and only short-lived in-memory telemetry is emitted. No object-store write occurs.
- If an account instead sets TTL=0 but keeps debug traces on, lightweight debug blobs may be written then garbage-collected within minutes; this is NOT the default and would require explicit customer enablement.

2) Residual data under default backup policy:
- Default cold backup retention is 90 days; after an approved deletion request residual copies in cold backups may remain until that 90-day retention window expires. Wording you can use: "Under Redwood's standard hosted backup policy, deleted objects are logically removed immediately; physical removal from cold backups occurs on the backup retention schedule (up to 90 days by default). Expedited purging from backups can be contracted with an agreed SLA and fee."

3) Example deletion confirmation JSON (sample):
{
  "deletion_request_id": "del-20290321-8a7f",
  "account": "VaultCorp",
  "affected_paths": ["s3://redwood-prod/vaultcorp/serving/payloads/2029/03/19/req-12345.bin"],
  "cache_invalidation_ids": ["cache-85f2"],
  "deleted_at": "2029-03-21T11:05:42-07:00",
  "notes": "Physical purge from backups scheduled per retention window (default 90 days). Signed attestation to follow."
}

If you want, we can paste the short Q&A block into the appendix and include the example JSON as an annex. I'll also attach a signed_attestation_vaultcorp.pdf draft once legal approves the wording.

Best —
Jordan
